scope: LSP byte-reader correctness, allocation retention and actual deterministic stdio subprocess integration. Not a real language server or total application RAM measurement.
protocolCases: Multibyte UTF-8 split at byte boundaries
Multiple coalesced frames and per-frame size bounds
Lazy geometric body allocation and exact small configured bounds
Dedicated retained allocation backing rather than shared Buffer-pool retention
Invalid or duplicated Content-Length, oversized header/body and truncated EOF
Callback failure/disposal and 100 partial-reader cleanup cycles
Concurrent Unicode completion/formatting replies and diagnostics over a real local stdio process
Invalid JSON-RPC top-level null and child stdout closure reject initialization, clear pending requests/listeners/buffers and stop the child

benchmark.limits: An untimed batch checks checksums and copy counts; timed runs check counts. No JSON parsing or actual language-server IO in parser timings. Full-suite activity had finished before the recorded benchmark; unrelated OS scheduling and frequency were not isolated.

remaining: Actual language-server indexing/cold-start tradeoffs, total Electron RAM under dirty editor/terminal/preview/provider workloads, broader stdout/IPC/PTY producer backpressure and cross-platform packaged measurements remain open.
